newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile sees at least 6 pct growth 2nd half - Garcia.
newsitem.headline: Chile sees at least 6 pct growth 2nd half - Garcia.

text.p: Chile can expect strong growth for the rest of the year, with the economy expected to expand by at least six percent in the second half, Economy Minister Alvaro Garcia said on Friday.

The growth is expected to be led by strong exports, with volume of shipments climbing 20.4 percent in the first four months of 1997 from year-earlier levels, he said. By value, exports grew 7.9 percent January to April this year.
"Our projections show that the economy will grow by more than six percent in the second half," Garcia said at a news conference.

The government has not decided whether to revise upward its official forecast of 5.8 percent growth this year, Garcia said, adding that more research was needed. The central bank forecasts growth at 5.5 percent to six percent.
Figures for the first few months of this year suggested a slowdown, with the Imacec index of economic growth showing a 3.4 percent rise in the first quarter.

To be sure, that figure was depressed by more than a full percentage point by severe drought in central Chile, the Central Bank said at the time. The drought is now widely seen as having ended after recent heavy rains in Santiago.
Exports appear to be strong, positioning the economy to return to a growth rate closer to last year's 7.1 percent, economists say.
Mining exports climbed 30 percent by volume in the first four months of the year, while industrial exports rose 16.7 percent and agricultural exports were up three percent, Garcia said.
Overall investment in the second half of the year will probably reach about 28.5 percent of gross domestic product, slightly higher than last year's rate, Garcia said.
